raw_text:
# 2-Week Hotel Room Maintenance Plan
**Client:** 32F, intermediate, Week 6 of 12-week hypertrophy block
**Equipment:** Yoga mat, door pull-up bar, plus improvised load (backpack, bed edge, chair, towel)
**Goal:** Preserve muscle and strength until she returns to Week 7

---

## The Principles Behind It

**Intensity matters more than volume.** Muscle can be maintained on roughly one-third to one-half of normal training volume, as long as sets are taken close to failure. That means fewer sets, but every working set ends at **0–2 reps in reserve (RIR)**. Without heavy load, effort is what keeps the stimulus.

**Make bodyweight harder with technique, not just reps.** She'll use four tools:
- **Tempo:** 3–4 second eccentrics and pauses in the stretched position
- **1.5 reps:** full rep plus a half rep from the bottom, counted as one rep
- **Unilateral work:** split squats and single-leg hinges roughly double the relative load
- **Backpack loading:** fill a backpack with water bottles, books, or a packed laptop bag (often 8–15 kg)

**Keep the frequency.** She trains four days a week in an upper/lower split. Each session runs 35–45 minutes, so it fits around a work trip.

**Be a good hotel neighbour.** There's no jumping. Everything is quiet and controlled.

**Check the bar.** Before the first session, she should confirm the door frame is solid (no hollow-core trim) and test the bar with a gradual bodyweight hang.

---

## Weekly Structure

| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| 1 | Upper A |
| 2 | Lower A |
| 3 | Rest / optional 15-min mobility |
| 4 | Upper B |
| 5 | Lower B |
| 6–7 | Rest or walking (aim for 8–10k steps; easy when exploring a new city) |

Days can shift around her schedule. Two rest days between sessions is fine. The aim is to hit each session once per week.

---

## Warm-Up (every session, 5 min)

- Cat-cow ×10
- World's greatest stretch ×5/side
- Scapular pull-ups (dead hang, depress shoulder blades) ×10
- Bodyweight squats ×15
- Glute bridges ×15
- One easy ramp-up set of the first exercise

---

## WEEK 1

### Upper A: Pull Emphasis
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Pull-ups (pronated) | 3 × 1–2 shy of failure | Rest 2–3 min. If she gets more than 12 reps, wear the loaded backpack |
| Deficit push-ups (hands on books or chair seats) | 3 × 8–15 | 3-sec lowering, 1-sec pause at bottom |
| Chin-up eccentrics | 2 × 5 | Jump or step to the top, then lower over 5 sec |
| Pike push-ups | 3 × 8–12 | Hips high, head travels forward of hands |
| Hanging scapular shrugs + knee raises | 2 × 10 + 10 | Shrug first, then knee raises in the same hang |
| Push-up 1.5 reps (finisher) | 1 × to 1 RIR | Bottom half-rep, then full rep = 1 |

### Lower A: Quad Emphasis
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Bulgarian split squat (rear foot on bed/chair) | 3 × 10–15/leg | Backpack loaded, 3-sec down. Rest 90 sec between legs |
| Heel-elevated goblet squat (backpack held at chest) | 3 × 15–25 | Heels on a book. 1.5 reps if 25 is easy |
| Single-leg hip thrust (shoulders on bed edge) | 3 × 10–15/leg | 2-sec squeeze at top |
| Reverse lunge to knee drive | 2 × 12/leg | Controlled, no hop |
| Sissy squat (holding door frame) | 2 × 8–12 | Regress to partial range if knees object |
| Single-leg calf raise off a stair/book | 3 × 15–20 | Full stretch at the bottom, 2-sec pause |

### Upper B: Push Emphasis
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Feet-elevated pike push-up (feet on bed) | 3 × 6–12 | Closest thing she has to an overhead press |
| Chin-ups (supinated) | 3 × 1–2 shy of failure | Add backpack if over 12 |
| Archer push-ups or ring-width push-ups | 3 × 6–10/side | Shift weight to one side |
| Bench/chair dips | 2 × 10–15 | Stop at about 90° elbow. Skip if her shoulders dislike them; replace with close-grip push-ups |
| Pull-up isometric holds | 3 × 15–30 sec | Chin over bar, then hold at 90° elbow on set 3 |
| Prone Y-T-W raises on mat | 2 × 8 each | Rear delt and mid-trap work in place of rows |

### Lower B: Posterior Chain Emphasis
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Single-leg Romanian deadlift (backpack in opposite hand) | 3 × 10–12/leg | 3-sec lowering, feel the hamstring stretch |
| Towel hamstring slider curls (on hard floor or bathroom tile) | 3 × 8–15 | Bridge up, slide heels out slowly, pull in. Single-leg if too easy |
| Cossack squats | 3 × 8/side | Builds adductor strength and mobility |
| Glute bridge 1.5 reps (backpack across hips) | 3 × 15–20 | |
| Step-ups onto sturdy chair or bed frame | 2 × 12/leg | Only if the surface is stable. Otherwise do split squat holds of 30 sec/leg |
| Hollow body hold | 3 × 20–40 sec | |

---

## WEEK 2: Same Structure, Small Progressions

Exercises stay the same so she isn't relearning movements. Progress **one** variable per exercise:

- **Pull-ups and chin-ups:** add backpack weight, or add a 3-sec eccentric to every rep.
- **Push-up variations:** move to a deeper deficit or to 1.5 reps.
- **Bulgarian split squats:** add a 2-sec pause at the bottom.
- **Single-leg RDLs:** add a pause at the bottom of each rep.
- **Slider curls:** progress to single-leg, or slow the eccentric to 4–5 sec.
- **Pike push-ups:** raise the feet higher, or add a 2-sec pause with the head near the floor.

**Volume stays the same.** Do not add sets. This is maintenance, and adding fatigue mid-trip only makes re-entry harder.

**Days 13–14:** do Lower B and Upper B at about 2–3 RIR instead of 0–1. This takes some fatigue off before she gets back to heavy loading.

---

## Optional Mobility Day (15 min)

- 90/90 hip switches ×10
- Couch stretch 60 sec/side (bed edge works)
- Thoracic rotations ×10/side
- Dead hang from the bar, 3 × 30 sec (good for shoulders and spine after flights)
- Deep squat hold, 2 × 60 sec

---

## Nutrition and Recovery While Traveling

- **Protein:** keep it at roughly **1.6–2.2 g/kg/day**. This matters most for muscle retention. Easy travel options are Greek yogurt, eggs, rotisserie chicken, jerky, protein bars, and a tub of whey or single-serve packets in the suitcase.
- **Calories:** aim for maintenance. A mild surplus from restaurant eating is fine. A big deficit is the main thing to avoid, since a deficit combined with reduced training raises the risk of muscle loss.
- **Sleep and jet lag:** if she crosses time zones, she should get daylight early, keep caffeine to the morning, and expect the first one or two sessions to feel flat.
- **Hydration:** flights and hotel air are drying, so she should be generous with water.
- **If the schedule collapses:** the minimum effective dose is **two full-body sessions per week**. Take the first two exercises from Upper A and Lower A one day, and the first two from Upper B and Lower B another day. That alone will hold most of her progress.

---

## Re-Entry: Resuming Week 7 of the Block

- **First session back:** use Week 6 loads, or about 5–10% lighter on the main lifts if she feels rusty, and hold reps at 2–3 RIR. Expect strength to be back within a session or two. Two weeks of reduced training rarely causes meaningful muscle loss, especially with this plan.
- **Sessions 2–3:** return to normal Week 7 programming.
- **Expect DOMS to return** with weighted eccentrics, particularly in the hamstrings and quads, because slider curls and split squats don't fully replicate barbell loading.
- **Scale weight may rise slightly** from glycogen and water once she's back on heavier training and regular food. That isn't fat gain.

---

**Summary for the client:** fewer sets, every set close to failure, the same four sessions both weeks, and enough protein. She'll come home ready to pick up Week 7.
